Composite checkpost Indicator: All new country spirit shop licenses issued through auction by FY2010. Progress/Status: One of the key focus areas in excise reforms is to introduce a regime in which the method of allotting licenses to country liquor shops is replaced by an auction-based system. In line with such policy measures, auctions of country liquor shops have taken place in Assam. In 15 districts, 189 country liquor shops out of the 203 shops have been settled through a competitive auction process based on the guidelines framed as a second tranche condition. The awards to the country spirit shops were given in March 2010 for a fresh term and were effective from April 2010. Data Source: Budget speeches of finance minister Target year: 2010

Progress/Status: As part of this process, the Revenue and Disaster Management Department has implemented the statewide rollout of the computerized registration process in 21 districts (all districts excluding the districts under autonomous councils). Following the signing of the contract with the implementation vendor in May 2011, work on the different activities has started in 21 districts which cover 70 subregistrar's offices (SROs). The site survey work and the site preparation activity has been completed in all the sites. The civil works have been completed in 70 SROs. Composite checkpost Indicator: Taxpayers under large taxpayer unit will file electronic VAT returns by FY2010. Progress/Status: The CTD has set up a large taxpayer unit (LTU) in each of the four commercial tax units in Guwahati.15 The LTU caters to dealers having a turnover of more than Rs100 million or a tax liability of more than Rs5 million. The joint commissioner of taxes has the responsibility of supervising and monitoring these units, which will each have a dedicated superintendent of taxes who will exclusively look after the work of the LTUs; other assistants have also been posted in these units. The LTUs have had a positive impact on the state revenue administration; the combined revenue collection by LTUs grew by 32.56% in FY2011 over FY2010. Compliance tracking has become more systematic, and proper assessment and scrutiny of the returns can be done on a regular basis. In view of the focused nature of work in the LTUs, it is now possible to efficiently manage dealers, who contribute the bulk of revenues. Data Source: Commercial taxes

Employee contributions to the pension fund Indicator: Agreement letter with fund manager by FY2009. Progress/Status: States have to confirm their illingness to participate in the NPS and agree to being governed by the NPS framework and other regulatory parameters, directions, egulations, and guidelines. Upon doing so, state governments need to enter into a separate agreement with the NPS Trust and the CRA, but they are not required to enter into separate agreements with the fund managers, as the NPS Trust has an agreement with its fund manager. Taking into consideration the NPS of the government of India, which enables state governments to better manage pension obligations under a regulated framework, the GOA has decided to join the NPS and enter into an agreement with the NPS Trust and the CRA. This obviated the need to enter into separate agreements with fund managers. This arrangement will facilitate a smooth transition from the old benefit scheme to the newly defined contribution scheme as soon as possible. The GOA signed separate agreements with the NPS Trust and the CRA on 29 October 2009. Data Source: Loan review missions Baseline year: 2009

Output: Component 4-Public Sector Enterprise Closure: 1. Financial closure of PSEs, 2. Established asset management cell, 3. Liquidation of assets of a selected PSE, 4. Training opportunities for employees of the PSEs notified for closure who are participating in VRS, 5. Statutory audit, 6. Labor rehabilitation plan Indicator: Clear debt management policy and detailed procedural manual by FY2009. Progress/Status: The debt management policy adopted by the GOA in August 2011 lays down the basic framework of public debt that is consistent with the medium-term fiscal framework and the statutory provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility and the Budget Management Act. The policy is based on the following parameters: (i) least cost, (ii) effective coordination with fiscal policies, (iii) operational structure, (iv) transparency and accountability, (v) performance parameters, and (vi) adoption of a proper risk management strategy. A debt management manual has been framed by the GOA for providing operational guidance to the staff associated with the debt management functions. The manual covers five broad areas: (i) theoretical foundations of public debt, (ii) the legal framework of debt, (iii) the institutional framework, (iv) sources of debt and their management, and (v) a risk management framework. Data Source: Loan review missions

The key end-of-program outcomes will include (i) increased tax buoyancy as a result of efficient revenue administration; (ii) expenditures prioritized to allow greater allocation for investments in, and maintenance of, assets; (iii) savings in debt servicing costs as a result of strengthened debt management capacities and consolidated policy procedures; and (iv) better mitigation of fiscal risk originating from selected loss-generating PSEs and further steps towards financial closure and initiation of legal closure process for PSEs notified for closure by getting the statutory audits completed and initating liquidation of assets.

Progressive reduction in budgetary allocation for PSEs, taking the budgetary allocation for FY2007 as the baseline figure. Progress/Status: All counterpart funds from the first tranche of $40 million had been disbursed for the VRS and related compensation. The Department of Public Enterprise prepared a statement on the unit-wise breakup of payment released under the VRS and number of employees involved, and then provided a status report on fund disbursement and other related matters in November 2009; $32 million out of the $40 million second tranche was released for payment of VRS and related compensation to employees of closed PSEs. In total, $78.13 million has been disbursed to employees who voluntarily retired from the 15 PSEs (as of September 2011) as against the $72 million disbursed from counterpart funding. Data Source: Statistical report on PSEs in Assam
